title: Amazon’s shopping agent now takes orders by text, with Sponsored Product ads in the replies
gist: Amazon's Alexa shopping agent now accepts orders via SMS for an invite-only group of U.S. customers, with Sponsored Product ads appearing inside those text conversations — though purchases the agent completes autonomously remain ad-free.

title: Amazon adds over 100 Alexa for Shopping functions
gist: Amazon has added over 100 new capabilities to Alexa for Shopping, covering registries, subscriptions, delivery, and billing; Amazon's CEO noted that users of the tool spend 50% more per order than non-users.

title: Walmart ramps up Sparky features in time for the holidays
gist: Walmart's AI assistant Sparky added features including shopping-list-to-cart conversion, visual recognition, and recipe generation ahead of the holidays; Walmart says Sparky users spend 40% more per order and usage is up 70% since launch.

title: Zalando sees new revenue potential in external shops
gist: Zalando is expanding its platform to surface products from external shops like Westwing, with an AI shopping agent eventually placing orders on those external sites directly from within the Zalando app.

title: EU Commission approves takeover Ceconomy by JD.com
gist: The European Commission has approved JD.com's acquisition of Ceconomy, owner of MediaMarkt and Saturn, with conditions requiring JD.com to offer warehousing and logistics services to third-party retailers.

title: JD Sports rolls out stock-tracking technology across 414 stores to tackle availability and theft
gist: JD Sports deployed RFID inventory tracking across 414 UK and Ireland stores in roughly three months, achieving 98% on-shelf availability and cutting replenishment times by 20%.

title: GUEST COMMENT Lidl is winning the high street. Can it win the agentic shopping era?
gist: A strategy piece examines how Lidl's physical-first, discount model may fare as AI shopping agents increasingly handle purchase decisions, arguing the retailer must choose between optimizing for agent-driven price comparison or investing in direct consumer relationships that agents can't easily replicate.

title: How TF is the grocery store a media channel?
gist: A sponsored guide from Grocery TV argues the physical grocery store remains a critical purchase-decision environment, citing that 95% of grocery shoppers make at least half their decisions in-store.

title: Hush opens first three standalone stores as it moves onto the high street
gist: UK womenswear brand Hush has opened its first three standalone stores after building its business primarily online, selecting three distinct retail environments to test different customer profiles.

title: Future of Marketing Briefing: Creators had a big year. Christmas still went to the celebrities
gist: Analysis of early holiday ad campaigns finds that despite creator marketing dominating brand strategies throughout the year, major Christmas campaigns from brands like John Lewis and Burberry are still led by celebrities rather than creators.

title: Glossy Pop Newsletter: Depop is hosting over 2,000 campus events this fall
gist: Depop has tripled its campus presence to over 300 colleges and is running more than 2,000 in-person events this fall through its Campus Manager ambassador program, targeting Gen Z sellers and buyers.

title: Big-Box Briefing: The themes that will dominate Jason Bonfig’s tenure as Best Buy’s new CEO
gist: Jason Bonfig, a 27-year Best Buy veteran, became CEO on November 1, succeeding Corie Barry, with his tenure expected to focus on accelerating the company's existing strategy.

title: Russia denies involvement in cyberattacks on supermarket fridges across Europe
gist: A wave of cyberattacks on supermarket refrigeration systems across Belgium, Sweden, Ireland, France, and the UK has forced retailers to discard large quantities of perishable food; Russia denied involvement despite two pro-Russian groups claiming responsibility.

title: US government warns of ‘ongoing cyber threat’ amid mass hacks of industrial retail and military freezers
gist: CISA, the FBI, and multiple U.S. federal agencies issued a joint warning about an ongoing cyber threat targeting internet-connected industrial refrigeration systems at grocery stores, cold storage facilities, military bases, and a blood bank, with attacks attributed broadly to Iran by security researchers.

title: How delivery apps came to be ‘discovery platforms’
gist: DoorDash is acquiring Instacart for $17 billion, a move that signals delivery apps like DoorDash, Uber, and Instacart are repositioning themselves as retail discovery platforms rather than pure logistics providers.

title: Bed Bath & Beyond’s new concept takes a page from original format
gist: Neighborhood Intelligence (parent of Bed Bath & Beyond, The Container Store, Kirkland's) is opening a standalone Bed Bath & Beyond store in Arizona, closing underperforming locations, and shifting focus to organic growth and global sourcing to improve margins. E-commerce revenue grew 9%, led by 75% growth from Overstock.com.

title: The Children’s Place shakes up leadership amid bankruptcy rumors
gist: The Children's Place is reportedly considering bankruptcy and possible liquidation, with four senior executives including the interim CEO departing amid declining sales and widening losses.

title: Under Armour to sell more full-price product at outlet stores
gist: Under Armour is restructuring its retail and product strategy—cutting SKUs by another 25%, adding full-price products to outlet stores, and licensing its youth sports category—as revenue fell 7% and analysts question whether the brand has a relevance problem beyond cyclical softness.

title: Reformation implements new AI planning tool, helping in-stock rates
gist: Reformation implemented an AI-backed demand-forecasting and planning tool that improved in-stock rates and full-price selling, contributing to 19% revenue growth in Q3 and an expansion of its active customer base by 23%.

title: As Barbie stumbles, Mattel cuts forecast ahead of the holidays
gist: Mattel posted 4% net sales growth in Q3 but cut its full-year guidance, citing underperformance of the Barbie brand and tariff uncertainty, as its new CEO faces pressure from investors to turn the business around.

title: Ramp data shows AI spending stalling just as Anthropic nears its IPO
gist: Ramp's spending data shows AI token volumes are rising but dollar spend flatlined in August–September, as price competition from OpenAI, Anthropic, and open-source models makes AI usage cheaper even as consumption grows.

title: Inside Oner Active’s tequila-scented new flagship in NYC
gist: Oner Active is opening its first NYC flagship store, with founder Krissy Cela deliberately positioning the brand away from wellness clichés — including a custom tequila-scented store fragrance — to create a distinct in-store identity.

title: Show HN: Coldframe, a honeypot that poses as a supermarket fridge controller
gist: A developer released an open-source Python honeypot that impersonates internet-exposed supermarket refrigeration controllers to log attacker behavior, credentials, and exploit attempts targeting real CVEs in Danfoss and Dixell systems.

title: After the midterms, things are looking rocky for Elon Musk and data centers
gist: Following a Democratic wave in U.S. midterm elections, nearly all ballot measures restricting data center construction passed, and newly elected officials in states like Texas have campaigned on limiting hyperscaler projects, while companies like OpenAI are already adjusting their community engagement policies in response.

title: ThredUp revenue growth slows despite record number of buyers
gist: ThredUp posted 7% revenue growth to $88.2M in Q3 but cut Q4 guidance sharply as average item prices fell from $21 to $18 and competitors ramped up promotions. Record buyer counts and order volumes couldn't offset lower spend-per-item and intensifying pressure from peer-to-peer rivals like Depop.

title: Amazon deploys thousands of smart glasses to delivery drivers
gist: Amazon is deploying 5,000 smart glasses to delivery drivers in 2026, expanding to 20,000+ by end of 2027, with the glasses surfacing navigation, delivery preferences, and proof-of-capture without drivers needing to check a handheld device.

title: Amazon debuts text-to-shop AI agent feature
gist: Amazon is rolling out a text-based shopping feature for Alexa for Shopping that lets customers add items to cart and complete purchases via SMS, including photo-based product discovery and price tracking. Consumer trust in AI-led purchase completion remains low despite growing usage for research.

title: How Azuna’s strong supply chain fuels its 9-figure sales
gist: DTC air-freshener brand Azuna has reached nine-figure annual online revenue by building supply chain resilience through long-term raw material contracts, owned manufacturing, and multi-tiered fulfillment rather than relying on third-party logistics.

title: Shopping or social? What an under-16 ban could mean for resale
gist: The UK government is weighing whether its proposed under-16 social media ban should extend to online marketplaces like eBay, Vinted, and Depop, whose social features — feeds, messaging, following — blur the line between commerce and social networking. Inclusion could affect both buyer demand and seller supply on resale platforms, and would likely trigger mandatory age verification requirements.

title: AI joins the Christmas ecommerce rush — but will recommendations turn into sales?
gist: Adobe forecasts UK festive online spending to hit £28.52bn, with AI-referred traffic to retail sites up 214% year-on-year during November–December. Consumer research shows AI is primarily used for gift inspiration and price comparison rather than autonomous purchasing, with only 8–19% willing to let AI complete purchases on their behalf.

title: Black Friday spending set to hit £9.8bn as shoppers plan Christmas bargains
gist: UK Black Friday spending is forecast to reach £9.8bn, up 3% year-on-year, with online retail capturing £5.29bn of that. Shopper sentiment has shifted sharply toward viewing Black Friday as a genuine savings event, with 63% calling it a good way to save versus 35% last year.

title: Exclusive: Ulta Beauty bets on health tracking with Oura in 1,000 stores
gist: Ulta Beauty is launching the Oura Ring 5 health tracker across 1,000 U.S. stores and online from mid-November, marking its first foray into wearable health tech. The move is driven by data showing 72% of Ulta's customer base already prioritizes daily wellness.

title: How enterprise brands are retooling commerce platforms to capture AI shoppers
gist: Shopify reports AI-referred traffic to its merchant storefronts up 2.6x year-on-year in Q3, with AI-referred orders up 3.3x and conversion rates 64% higher than organic search. The article argues that winning in agentic commerce requires three things from retailers: structured product data legibility, multi-channel reach, and preserved customer identity through checkout.

title: Beyond the AI shortlist: How brands can inspire the next purchase
gist: As AI agents increasingly build shopping shortlists from structured product data, brands face two distinct challenges: winning the AI recommendation through machine-readable, semantically rich product attributes, and then converting the AI-referred shopper on the product page through visualization, fit confidence, and consistent information. Only 46% of consumers fully trust AI recommendations and 89% double-check before buying.

title: Peak season 2026: What’s changed, and how do you win?
gist: Research from Cardlytics shows UK shoppers are managing budgets tightly even during the festive season, trading down and breaking brand loyalties, but still spending when prompted by relevant, timely offers. The article frames peak 2026 success as a relevance and timing challenge rather than a demand problem.

title: Poundland blocked from buying new stock despite £86m turnaround
gist: Poundland has been blocked from ordering new stock by owner Gordon Brothers, which restricted cash access despite the retailer swinging from an EBITDA loss of £68.1m to a profit of £18.1m in the past year. The company faces administration if a rescue deal isn't secured before its notice of intention to appoint administrators expires on 13 November.

title: Ikea sales fall for third year as it slashes prices to revive growth
gist: Ikea reported a third consecutive year of declining global sales, down 2% to €43.8bn, and is responding with a €1.2bn investment in price cuts of up to 25% across 1,000+ products in Europe alongside a push to open smaller city-centre stores. Weak consumer confidence in China and the Middle East, plus rising freight and energy costs, are cited as ongoing headwinds.

title: Amazon launches AI shopping through text messages in agentic push
gist: Amazon has launched text-based AI shopping through Alexa for Shopping, allowing US customers to search, compare, and purchase products via SMS with the assistant remembering preferences and previous orders. The rollout is part of Amazon's broader agentic commerce push, with agentic feature usage up eightfold since the start of the year.

title: As publishers await click data, Google’s AI visibility push complicates the opt-out decision
gist: Google is developing a Search Console opt-out that lets publishers exclude their content from AI Overviews, following a UK CMA requirement, while simultaneously enhancing AI Overviews to make opting out less commercially attractive. Publishers are waiting for click data to understand the traffic impact before deciding.

title: ChatGPT is about to show brands their mention count
gist: OpenAI is testing an analytics dashboard inside ChatGPT that lets businesses track how often they appear in ChatGPT answers and how many clicks those mentions generate, with a Shopify store connection as one verification route. The tool is part of an unreleased Business Hub that also includes a business agent feature.

title: Exclusive: TikTok Shop launches a paid premium tier for 1M of its top US shoppers
gist: TikTok Shop launched a paid membership pilot called TikTok Shop Plus, offering free shipping, exclusive discounts, and instant refunds for $9.99/month to over 1 million of its most loyal U.S. customers. The move mirrors Amazon Prime and Walmart+ and signals TikTok Shop's push to deepen loyalty as it holds roughly 20% of the U.S. social-commerce market.

title: Reddit is turning user conversations into AI-powered product reviews
gist: Reddit launched 'Reddit Reviews,' an AI-powered feature that aggregates and summarizes user conversations about products into structured review pages covering ~10,000 products, now live for all U.S. users. The feature is designed to position Reddit as a product research destination ahead of the holiday season, though it may also attract brand astroturfing.

title: Singles Day spend set to top £2.2bn as UK shoppers embrace global retail event
gist: UK consumers are forecast to spend over £2.2bn during Singles Day 2025, up roughly 10% year over year, as the event grows beyond its Chinese origins and increasingly marks the start of the UK peak shopping season. Retailers including ASOS, AliExpress, and Temu are extending promotions beyond November 11 into multi-week campaigns.

title: Target vs. Walmart: Holiday marketing’s stakes feel higher this year
gist: Walmart and Target are both anchoring their 2025 holiday campaigns around narrative storytelling rather than pure price messaging, as both retailers compete for the same value-conscious but higher-income shopper. Analysts note Target is leaning into personalization and a unified creator/influencer strategy as its key differentiator against Walmart's scale.

title: Holiday hiring looks different this year. Here’s why.
gist: Retailers are quietly scaling back large seasonal hiring announcements, instead relying on existing staff, on-demand pools, and part-time roles — with Amazon as the notable outlier, planning to hire 300,000+ seasonal workers, up 20% from recent years. The shift from seasonal to part-time labels suggests some employers expect demand to persist well beyond Q4.

title: The Children’s Place, in search of new ownership, files for bankruptcy
gist: The Children's Place filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy with over $881 million in debts, citing declining demand, inflation, tariffs, and intensifying competition from Target, Walmart, and Amazon in value-priced children's apparel. The company is running store-closing sales while seeking a buyer by year-end, with bids due December 9.

title: HURR reaches profitability for the first time
gist: Fashion rental marketplace HURR has reached profitability for the first time after 18 months of operational restructuring, cost scrutiny, and strategic changes led by founder Lauren Roberts. The milestone is being framed as proof that circular fashion business models can be commercially viable, not just mission-driven.

title: Asda turnaround falters as market share slips to 11.3%
gist: Asda is the only major UK grocer to report falling sales in the latest 12-week period, with revenue down 0.5% year-on-year and market share dropping from 11.6% to 11.3%, while rivals including Lidl, Morrisons, and Ocado all grew. Newly appointed CEO David Potts faces the task of reversing the decline under Asda's Formula for Growth strategy.

title: Mars wants to future proof impulse buys as AI is poised to take over more grocery runs
gist: Mars is actively strategizing around agentic AI shopping assistants potentially replacing impulse-driven grocery runs, working to ensure its snack brands remain discoverable and purchasable when AI agents, rather than humans, make routine buying decisions. The company published a future-of-shopping report with Kantar and Synthesis to map the shift.

title: Mattel brings Barbie, Hot Wheels to TikTok Shop
gist: Mattel is launching a branded storefront on TikTok Shop with around 20 products across its major toy properties, marking its first direct sales on the platform as it aims to convert existing community engagement into commerce. The company plans to expand to over 40 products and sees TikTok Shop as a channel for discovery and education alongside traditional retail.

title: OpenAI’s new business agents give brands a free way into the conversation it’s also selling as an ad
gist: OpenAI has launched a Business Hub where brands can claim a verified profile and, for U.S. e-commerce and online services businesses, publish a free 'business agent' — a branded chat within ChatGPT — alongside a paid ad version of the same format. The free organic option gives brands a way into AI-driven conversations before the paid product fully rolls out.

title: European Council approves VAT simplification for online sales
gist: The European Council has approved an expansion of the digital VAT Import One Stop Shop (IOSS) to cover high-value goods sold online, simplifying VAT compliance for platforms and suppliers operating across EU markets. The move is part of broader EU efforts to streamline VAT collection on cross-border e-commerce.

title: Almost half of shoppers plan Black Friday purchases in advance, with AI and social media having limited influence on buying behaviour
gist: YouGov research of 2,000+ UK online shoppers finds that 47% already know what they intend to buy before major events like Black Friday, while only 9% say social media and 5% say AI recommendations meaningfully drive additional unplanned purchases. The findings suggest retailers should focus on capturing pre-formed intent rather than relying on promotions or digital channels to generate new demand.

title: EU targets online sales tricks with Digital Fairness Act
gist: The European Commission has proposed the Digital Fairness Act to ban dark patterns, addictive design, and deceptive influencer marketing in online sales across the EU.

title: USPS Service Cuts Could Impact Merchants
gist: USPS posted a $6.5B net loss in fiscal 2026 and its Postmaster General warned of potential post office closures and reduced Marketing Mail service levels, with formal proposals expected in Q1 2027.

title: Shein’s total investment in Poland reaches 1 billion euros
gist: Shein has committed an additional €500M to expand its logistics center in Poland, bringing its total investment in the country to €1B since 2022.

title: United Airlines bans AI agents from booking flights on behalf of travelers
gist: United Airlines is banning third-party AI agents from booking flights on its platforms, citing security risks, potential regulatory violations, and the desire to avoid adding powerful new intermediaries to its sales funnel.

title: Amazon’s Black Friday, Cyber Monday deals boast record exclusives
gist: Amazon's Black Friday and Cyber Monday events (Nov. 19–30) will feature a record number of Amazon-exclusive deals and lean heavily on AI-powered personalization through Alexa for Shopping, including price tracking and auto-buy features.

title: Big Box Briefing: How Target’s and Walmart’s beauty department makeovers are reshaping brand strategies
gist: Target and Walmart are overhauling their beauty and wellness aisles to compete with specialty retailers, forcing both large CPG companies and independent brands to rethink their distribution, media spend, and in-store presentation strategies.

title: Vinted looks to cash in on US expansion with new advertising push
gist: Vinted is expanding its post-purchase advertising business to the US via a partnership with Rokt, serving third-party brand offers immediately after checkout, replicating a model it has run across European markets since 2024 with a reported 4% average customer engagement rate.

title: Dr Martens faces make-or-break Christmas as UK sales plunge 21%
gist: Dr Martens reported a 9.2% revenue decline and a widened adjusted pre-tax loss for H1, with UK sales falling 21.3%, blaming weak boot demand, a hot summer, and planned DTC operational changes, while warning that full-year results hinge heavily on Christmas trading.

title: JD.com eyes European electronics dominance as $2.5bn takeover completes
gist: JD.com has completed its $2.5bn acquisition of Ceconomy, gaining control of MediaMarkt and Saturn across 11 European markets, with plans for next-day and 90-minute delivery and integration with its Joybuy e-commerce platform.

title: D+ Research: Marketers express revenue optimism for 2026 holiday season despite economic pressures
gist: A Digiday+ survey of 90 brand and retailer professionals found that 76% expect their 2026 holiday revenue to increase compared to 2025, a notably more optimistic outlook than last year's conservative forecasts.

title: GUEST COMMENT Retailers have work to do earning customer trust in AI
gist: Research from Sinch finds that while 81% of consumers trust AI for order tracking, only 62% are comfortable with AI handling payment or billing changes, and just 43% believe AI will make shopping easier overall, with 69% of retail organizations having rolled back AI agents due to governance failures.

title: 67% of shoppers will trade delivery speed for lower costs
gist: New UK research from Scurri finds that 67% of shoppers will accept slower delivery in exchange for free or cheaper shipping during Peak, while 61% prioritize free delivery versus just 29% prioritizing next-day — suggesting the holiday fulfillment battle is shifting from speed to cost and delivery certainty.

title: The Q4 playbook assumes shoppers start with search. Many no longer do.
gist: Salesforce data shows that between August 2025 and May 2026, discovery through brand-owned properties fell 7% and traditional search fell 15%, while discovery via AI assistants and social channels grew 38%, fundamentally disrupting the standard Q4 search-and-retargeting playbook.

title: BNPL bolsters holiday budgets
gist: A survey by ETA and TSG found that 20% of consumers plan to increase BNPL use this holiday season, while 47% don't plan to use it at all; tap-to-pay (53%) and digital wallets (31%) saw far higher adoption trial rates over the past year than BNPL (9%).

title: Walmart more than doubles planned drone delivery sites
gist: Walmart is adding 300 new drone delivery sites through an expanded partnership with Zipline, bringing its total planned drone locations to at least 570 — nearly nine times its current footprint — with deliveries possible in 30 minutes or less.

title: Brands are banking on live shopping this holiday season
gist: Brands are increasing investment in live shopping for the 2026 holiday season, with US livestream retail sales projected to reach nearly $20 billion this year and annual spend per buyer growing 23% to an average of $339.

title: ChatGPT’s new Wallet lets AI agents shop and check out for you
gist: OpenAI launched a ChatGPT Wallet that lets AI agents complete purchases on behalf of users, using payment tokens and biometric confirmation, initially for a limited set of U.S. Pro subscribers. The company also published a Commerce Partner Playbook for retailers wanting to support agentic shopping, as Amazon has already moved to block third-party agents.

title: The in-store shopping experience is broken. Can we fix it?
gist: Modern Retail podcast discussion on the most frustrating aspects of in-store shopping — including locked merchandise and confusing self-checkout — and how retailers are (or aren't) solving them through technology and store design.

title: Show Online What Shoppers Can’t Touch
gist: A practical guide showing how online merchants can communicate product texture and physical properties through photography — using light, in-use shots, and transformation imagery — since shoppers can't touch products online.

title: Lutnick Pushed to Weaken Chip Rules That Overlap with His Family Business
gist: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is accused of advocating for weaker chip export controls affecting Southeast Asian data centers, some of which are clients of Cantor Fitzgerald — the firm his sons now lead. Critics say he is using his regulatory role to protect business interests tied to his family.

title: Where was Nvidia’s security team?
gist: Following Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia over an affair with an executive at a Singapore data center company under U.S. investigation for chip smuggling, questions are emerging about what Nvidia's security team knew and whether it could have flagged the espionage risk. Corporate security experts say most U.S. companies are dangerously unprepared for China's long-horizon intelligence tactics.

title: Elon Musk, other tech execs sign petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang
gist: A petition signed by over 115,000 people — including Elon Musk, Garry Tan, and thousands of Nvidia employees and shareholders — is calling on Nvidia's board to reinstate Jensen Huang pending an independent investigation into the circumstances of his removal. Huang resigned after admitting to an affair with a chip executive suspected by U.S. intelligence of being a Chinese spy.

title: Asian governments react to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s exit
gist: Governments across Asia — including South Korea, Taiwan, Japan, Singapore, and China — are responding to Jensen Huang's Nvidia exit by seeking reassurance on chip supply commitments and monitoring implications for local AI projects. Singapore's investigation into Megaspeed and related individuals remains ongoing, while China rejected espionage allegations as groundless.

title: This year, every day is Black Friday
gist: Deal-seeking consumers are spreading holiday shopping across the entire season rather than concentrating it on a single day, yet Black Friday itself still holds outsized importance for retailers.

title: Black Friday sales tipped to hit £12.8bn but smaller retailers face profits wipeout
gist: UK online spending during the Black Friday period is forecast to reach £12.8bn, up 5% year-on-year, but heavy discounting and return costs — which can consume up to 66% of an item's value — threaten to wipe out profits for smaller retailers.

title: Beauty meets big-ticket tech: the battle for Black Friday demand
gist: Beauty is forecast to be the fastest-growing category over UK Black Friday weekend, with 45% of shoppers planning beauty purchases, though uneven search demand across brands signals that category growth doesn't automatically translate to individual brand wins.

title: GUEST COMMENT Black Friday is commerce media’s moment – are brands ready?
gist: Retail media investment is growing — 73% of buyers increased spend in the past year — but brands risk going dark on Black Friday if they don't pre-agree contingency budgets and monitor campaigns in real time, as traffic spikes can exhaust sponsored placements in hours.

title: ANALYSIS It’s Christmaaaas… but can retailers turn festive buzz into sales?
gist: UK retailers' 2026 Christmas ad campaigns are increasingly built to feed shoppable ecosystems and first-party data capture rather than pure brand awareness, with M&S and Boots rated highest for omnichannel and retail media integration respectively.

title: J. Crew introduces AI-powered Style Advisor
gist: J. Crew has launched an AI-powered Style Advisor built with Anthropic that functions as a desktop styling assistant, going beyond individual product search to offer outfit-level recommendations.

title: Toy sales aren’t just about kids anymore
gist: U.S. toy industry dollar sales grew 20% in the first nine months of the year, driven by adult collectors and fandom purchases rather than traditional children's toys.

title: Battling turnaround fatigue, Nike teases innovation pipeline
gist: Nike is signaling a turnaround through an upcoming innovation pipeline, including a revamped training category and a new manufacturing process for its Air franchise, as it works to overcome what the company acknowledges as turnaround fatigue.

title: How beauty and wellness leaders are prioritizing GEO and TikTok Shop
gist: Beauty and wellness brand leaders at a Glossy summit discussed shifting focus from SEO to generative engine optimization (GEO) and debated the growing importance of TikTok Shop for customer acquisition.

title: IKEA blames UK’s high business taxes as it scales back store expansion plans
gist: IKEA has scaled back planned UK store openings, citing what it describes as the highest business tax burden in Europe, even as UK sales edged up 0.5% to £2.26bn for FY26.

title: Uber and Zipline’s drone delivery service takes off in Texas, with dozens of cities to follow
gist: Uber Eats and Zipline have launched commercial drone delivery for food orders in Spring, Texas, with plans to expand to dozens of U.S. cities and reach one million deliveries per day by end of 2029.

title: Holiday shoppers expect AI to save them over $190 this year
gist: A survey finds holiday shoppers expect AI tools to save them over $190 this season by helping find deals and saving time, but warns AI should only promise what retailers can actually deliver.

title: Target traffic rises as retailer reports broad-based gains
gist: Target reported 5% traffic growth in Q3 and plans up to $6 billion in capital expenditures next year, signaling broad-based recovery across the retailer.

title: Brands booking creators to make their ads are pushing up $116B global influencer market
gist: Global creator marketing spend is projected to hit $116 billion in 2026 and grow at 12% annually through 2030, twice the rate of overall ad spending, driven largely by brands boosting creator content across paid channels.

title: Over two-fifths of shoppers will focus Golden Quarter spending on discounting events
gist: UK research finds 43% of shoppers plan to concentrate Christmas spending in promotional events, price remains the top purchase driver for 63% for the fourth straight year, and discount retailers like Aldi and Lidl are taking share from mainstream grocers.

title: ThredUp launches TikTok Shop livestreams as part of its social commerce push
gist: ThredUp has launched TikTok Shop livestreams filmed from its distribution centers, committing to 10 shows per week with plans to double that, with 75% of buyers being new to the platform and earlier Whatnot shows yielding median prices 52% above comparable marketplace listings.

title: Google's AI answers reducing search traffic by 40%
gist: A randomized experiment found Google's AI Overviews reduce clicks to outside websites by roughly 40%, and AI Overviews now appear on over 61% of tracked US keywords, up from 6% two years ago; meanwhile AI assistants collectively sent only 0.28% of web traffic in March 2026.

title: Google expands access to Gemini Tasks, which can help with calls, purchases
gist: Google is expanding Gemini's Tasks feature to hundreds of millions of free users, enabling the AI to make phone calls, complete purchases via Google Pay, and sign into websites on a user's behalf.

title: How brands can welcome AI users onto their sites this holiday season
gist: A Retail Dive piece argues that as more customers arrive on retail sites via AI tools this holiday season, the on-site experience needs to feel seamless and guide them toward completing a purchase.

title: Nike won’t return to growth for 3 more years
gist: Nike outlined a plan to grow revenue by $5 billion between fiscal 2027 and 2031, but projects two more years of revenue declines before any growth begins.

title: Home Depot names longtime company vet as CEO
gist: Home Depot has named CFO Richard McPhail, a company veteran since 2005, as its next CEO, with Ann-Marie Campbell becoming COO.

title: Target’s Black Friday sale includes in-store gift card giveaway
gist: Target's Black Friday sale will include in-store gift card giveaways and early deal access for paid membership customers, targeting budget-conscious shoppers.

title: In Graphic Detail: Welcome to the agentic commerce quarter
gist: AI-powered shopping agents are moving from experiment to infrastructure: OpenAI launched a ChatGPT wallet for agent purchases, Google is rolling out checkout via AI Mode in Canada, Walmart added agent spending caps, and Bain estimates one in four shoppers plan to start holiday shopping on an AI platform.

title: An Interview With Eric Seufert About Agentic Commerce
gist: Paywalled Stratechery interview with Eric Seufert on agentic commerce, touching on why advertising may win in the agent era and what it means for retailers to cater to AI agents rather than human browsers.

title: The AI agent boom is creating a new product data challenge for retailers
gist: A whitepaper from Akeneo warns that deploying multiple AI agents across the product lifecycle is fundamentally different from deploying one, and that competitive advantage will come not from the agents themselves but from having governed, structured, and trustworthy product data underneath them.

title: Target’s AI shopping assistant is driving sales
gist: Target's CEO says its beta AI shopping assistant, Ask Target, is showing early signs of driving sales in initial testing.

title: E-commerce boosts Home Depot, Lowe’s in Q3
gist: Home Depot and Lowe's both reported double-digit e-commerce growth in Q3, crediting continued investments in their digital shopping experiences.

title: Traffic recovery at T.J. Maxx, Marshalls boost TJX in Q3 as pressures mount
gist: TJX (T.J. Maxx, Marshalls) posted modest Q3 gains on recovering store traffic, but faces mounting competition from resale platforms, department store promotions, and Ross.

title: Economic optimism plunges to lowest level since Great Recession
gist: Gallup data shows public economic optimism has fallen to its lowest level since the Great Recession, with consumer perception increasingly diverging from GDP since the 2022 inflation spike.

title: Satya Nadella predicts AI agents will reshuffle the economics of the web
gist: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella argued at DealBook that the rise of AI agents will reshuffle internet economics, shifting revenue models from ad-driven human traffic toward transactional payments, and that platforms like Amazon blocking agents risk ceding ground to those that embrace them.

title: Walmart’s e-commerce boom driven by fulfillment speed
gist: Walmart U.S. e-commerce grew 23% in Q3, with fulfillment speed cited as the primary competitive differentiator.

title: Walmart’s convenience lures high-income shoppers
gist: Walmart is attracting higher-income shoppers by combining low prices with fast fulfillment, drone delivery, and a bundled Walmart+/Sam's Club membership, shifting its value proposition beyond cost alone.

title: Instagram creators can now add Amazon affiliate links directly to Reels, posts
gist: Instagram now lets creators add up to 30 Amazon affiliate product links directly to Reels or 20 to posts, earning commission with no cut taken by Instagram.

title: On is making a bigger play for American shoppers, one store at a time
gist: Swiss sportswear brand On is expanding its U.S. DTC retail footprint to 23 stores by end of 2026, using physical locations to build brand awareness and push beyond footwear into apparel and accessories.

title: JD Sports cuts profit outlook again as UK sales fall and French unrest hits trading
gist: JD Sports cut its full-year profit forecast for the second time in four months after group like-for-like sales fell 2.6% in Q3, citing weak footwear demand, a promotional market, civil unrest in France, and pressure on younger shoppers.

title: Retail sales bounce back as shoppers stock up on emergency supplies
gist: UK retail sales rose 0.7% month-on-month in October, beating forecasts, driven by emergency preparedness stockpiling and cooler weather boosting clothing; online sales grew 9.7% year-on-year and accounted for 29.2% of total retail spend.

title: Poundland owner accused of blocking tax payments as £60m remains out of reach
gist: Poundland owner Gordon Brothers has reportedly twice refused to authorize tax payments to HMRC despite the retailer holding £60m in cash, leaving shelves short and sales running 20–25% below target with 11,000 jobs at risk before a November 26 creditor protection deadline.

title: Poundland sales suffer as £60m cash row intensifies
gist: Poundland faces a cash access standoff with owner Gordon Brothers, pushing sales 20–25% below target during the pre-Christmas period, with a rescue deal needed before November 28 or administrators could break up the business.

title: Bath & Body Works CEO: ‘We are on track, but far from satisfied’
gist: Bath & Body Works marked one year of its Consumer First Formula strategy and is targeting a return to sustainable growth in 2027, with the CEO acknowledging progress but signaling dissatisfaction with current performance.

title: Gap Inc. is betting on ‘fashiontainment’ to fuel growth
gist: Gap Inc. reported Q3 net sales up 2% to $4 billion, with the Gap brand up 11% driven by Gen Z acquisition, while Athleta dropped 14% and Banana Republic fell 3%; the company is leaning into 'fashiontainment' as a growth lever.

title: Former Alibaba exec’s Everful raises $48.5M to connect retailers with Chinese factories
gist: Everful, a startup connecting smaller retailers and brands directly to Chinese factories with end-to-end sourcing, quality control, and logistics, raised $48.5M Series A and is on track for $100M annualized revenue, with a Shopify integration and plans to expand in the U.S. and Europe.

title: Big-Box Briefing: Target faces off with Trader Joe’s, Quince and HomeGoods
gist: Target posted 5.6% comparable sales growth in Q3 under new CEO Michael Fiddelke, though analysts note the result is more modest when stacked against weaker 2024 comparisons following a difficult 2025.
